Keywords: headline, h1, hero copy, main claim, tagline
Formula: [Specific offer] for [specific audience] + the differentiating qualifier
Good Example: Chest, lung and sleep medicine in Bhopal
Truth Constraint: The claim must be something the client actually delivers today, not aspirationally

Formula: Who it is for + what changes + the proof anchor
Good Example: Consultation, testing and bronchoscopy for asthma, COPD and sleep apnoea. 18 years of practice, MD in Chest Medicine.
Bad Example: We provide world-class healthcare solutions with cutting-edge technology and a patient-first approach
Truth Constraint: Every number and credential in the subhead must appear again, sourced, later on the page

Formula: Category or context word; never a sentence
Truth Constraint: Must describe the section accurately; not a keyword-stuffing slot

Keywords: cta, button, action label, primary action
Formula: Verb + the object the visitor receives
Truth Constraint: The label must match exactly what happens next. 'Book' must lead to booking, not a contact form

Keywords: reassurance, microcopy, under button, friction reducer
Formula: What happens after the click + the timeframe you can meet
Good Example: Confirmation within one working day. No payment required to hold a slot.
Bad Example: We will get back to you as soon as possible
Truth Constraint: Never promise a response time the client has not agreed to

Formula: The question the section answers, phrased as the visitor thinks it
Truth Constraint: One idea. If it needs 'and', it is two sections

Keywords: service, offering, card copy, treatment, capability
Formula: [What it is] + [who it is for or when it applies]
Good Example: Sleep study. Overnight monitoring for snoring, daytime sleepiness and suspected apnoea.
Bad Example: Comprehensive solutions tailored to your unique needs
Truth Constraint: Only list services actually offered at the stated locations

Good Example: MD Chest Medicine, Bombay Hospital Institute of Medical Sciences, 2008
Truth Constraint: Client-supplied and verifiable. Never generate, infer, or expand an abbreviation you have not been given
Requires a period and a source. Unsourced numbers do not ship

Formula: Direct answer in sentence one; the qualifier or exception in sentence two
Good Example: Yes. Walk-ins are seen between 10am and 12pm on weekdays, though booked appointments are prioritised. Evening slots are appointment-only.
Bad Example: Please contact us for more information regarding our availability
Truth Constraint: Answers must survive being quoted alone in a search result or an AI answer

Formula: Facts first: role, years, training, focus. Character second: why this work.
Good Example: Dr. Sharma has practised respiratory medicine for 18 years, training at NITRD Delhi and teaching at RKDF Medical College.
Bad Example: With a passion for excellence and a commitment to innovation, we strive to be the best
Truth Constraint: Third-person or first-person consistently. No unverifiable superlatives

Keywords: product copy, flavour, item description, variant
Formula: Sensory or functional specifics + the material fact
Good Example: Kala khatta. Black salt, cumin and jamun syrup, carbonated hard. 200ml returnable glass.
Bad Example: A delightful taste experience that will tantalise your senses
Truth Constraint: Ingredients and volumes must match the label. No health or nutrition claims without label evidence

Keywords: privacy, data note, consent, form footer
Formula: What is collected + what it is used for + who sees it
Good Example: We use your number only to confirm this appointment. It is not shared or added to any marketing list.
Bad Example: Your privacy is important to us
Truth Constraint: Must describe the actual data flow. If the form emails a third-party inbox, say so

Formula: What went wrong + what the visitor can do now + the fallback channel
Good Example: That did not send. Try again, or call +91 83490 31096 — the line is open until 6pm.
Truth Constraint: Never blame the visitor. Always provide a second route to the same outcome

Keywords: empty, no results, nothing here, zero state
Formula: What is missing + the reason + the next useful action
Good Example: No stockists in Indore yet. Nearest is Bhopal, 190km — or order online.
Truth Constraint: Do not present an empty state as a temporary loading state

Keywords: disclaimer, regulated, medical claim, financial claim
Formula: State the limit of the claim plainly in the visitor's language
Good Example: This page describes services offered. It is not medical advice and does not replace consultation.
Truth Constraint: Draft for the client to review. Never assert compliance with a regulation you have not verified
